title: How to use the CSSBuy shipping calculator before and after packing
summary: Use parcel dimensions, actual weight and the selected route’s rules to understand what an estimate can tell you at each stage.

sections.heading: Start with the question your estimate can answer
paragraphs: A buyer looking at a fleece jacket and a pair of shoes usually wants a single number for shipping. At this point the useful question is smaller. Could a plausible parcel containing these items travel by a route you would actually choose, at a cost you could accept? The CSSBuy shipping calculator lets you explore that question. Keep your first result as a planning estimate, with the date, destination and assumptions beside it. You will have better inputs once the goods have reached the warehouse.

Before opening the calculator, write down how many units you intend to buy and which packaging you want to keep. A listing that gives the length of a jacket has given you a garment measurement. It tells you very little about the height of a packed jacket. A seller who can give you the dimensions of one boxed pair of shoes has answered a more useful question, although the international carton may still be larger. Mark each input as measured, supplied by a seller, or your own estimate.

sections.heading: Use the units beside each field
paragraphs: Keep dimensions together in one unit and weight in the unit the form requests. For instance, a carton measuring 420 by 300 by 200 millimetres measures 42 by 30 by 20 centimetres. A weight of 2,400 grams is 2.4 kilograms. Entering 420 in a field intended for centimetres changes the assumed length tenfold. It is easy to overlook a unit mismatch on a small screen, especially when a supplier has given you dimensions and weight in different systems.

Enter the destination of the final recipient and the attributes that describe the actual contents. Check the route details for size and contents restrictions before comparing prices. An attractive result for clothing gives you little useful information about sending a different mix of goods. If the form returns no suitable route, verify the units and the inputs against the listing. Then ask CSSBuy about that specific combination of destination, contents and dimensions. Changing the contents description merely to obtain a displayed price leaves your original question unanswered.

sections.heading: Calculate where volume starts to matter
paragraphs: The scale tells you how heavy the packed parcel is. Dimensional weight expresses the space that the parcel occupies as a weight. When a route uses centimetres and publishes a divisor for cubic centimetres per kilogram, multiply the three external dimensions and divide by that divisor. Read the selected route’s own treatment of the resulting weight, including any thresholds and rounding. Carry your unrounded answer through the calculation until you reach that step.

Consider an illustrative route that charges on the greater of scale weight and volume divided by 6,000. This divisor is a teaching assumption. A box measuring 40 by 30 by 24 centimetres occupies 28,800 cubic centimetres. Its dimensional weight under that assumption is 4.8 kilograms. If the box weighs 3.1 kilograms on the scale, volume sets the starting weight for pricing. Compressing the height to 18 centimetres produces 3.6 kilograms of dimensional weight, assuming the same footprint. The arithmetic describes one parcel under one rule, without assigning it a CSSBuy rate.

There is an especially useful follow-up calculation. Multiply the scale weight by the divisor and divide by the footprint of the box. In the example, 3.1 multiplied by 6,000 and divided by 1,200 gives 15.5 centimetres. Around that height, scale weight would start to dominate. Below that point, reducing height further might achieve nothing for the chargeable weight. This gives you a concrete reason to decline further compression when it could damage the item.

sections.heading: Compare route results on the same parcel
paragraphs: Use the same outer dimensions, gross weight, contents and destination for your first route comparison. Record the route name, displayed currency, quoted amount and any timing information you care about. Read the conditions associated with each result. A low headline amount on a service that cannot carry the contents, exceeds your acceptable delivery window or requires a smaller carton does not solve the delivery problem. Eliminate those routes before trying to rank the remaining choices.

Check how the route prices its first unit and subsequent units if that information appears. Under a hypothetical tariff that rounds every additional half kilogram upward, a small increase near a boundary can move a parcel into another price band. Under a different tariff the same increase might leave the quote unchanged. Use calculator runs on either side of your estimated weight to see where the actual quote changes. Avoid interpolating a price per kilogram from a screenshot of another person’s parcel.

sections.heading: Run a useful pair of estimates before purchasing
paragraphs: Make your first scenario the parcel you would most like to receive. Suppose you want the shoes in their retail box and would accept a moderately compressed fleece. Record which dimensions came from the seller and which you estimated. In a second run change only the uncertain factor most likely to alter the price, perhaps the final height once the fleece is added. Keeping the other inputs fixed makes it possible to explain the difference between the results.

If both amounts fit your budget, you have learned that this particular uncertainty matters little to your decision. If only the smaller estimate works, identify what would have to happen to reach it. For example, ask whether the retail box can be folded while keeping the shoes protected. A buyer who needs the undamaged box as part of a gift should use the intact-box scenario when deciding whether to buy. Save the acceptable option and the reason you chose it beside the product link.

sections.heading: Replace assumptions with warehouse measurements
paragraphs: After arrival, check the warehouse records against your original list. Note any missing unit, substitution or change in the packaging you intend to keep. Individual item weights can help you identify a bad early estimate, but adding those weights still leaves the outer carton and protective material unaccounted for. Request the measurements available for the combined packing arrangement if the difference would affect your choice. Include the box, protective insert or other object whose dimensions matter in that request.

Run the calculator again with the measured external dimensions and gross weight. Read the parcel submission screen for the amount you are actually being asked to fund. CSSBuy’s Buy For Me guide describes an estimated shipping deposit and a subsequent reconciliation. Keep the estimate, deposit and final charge in separate entries. When a figure changes, you can then tell whether the change happened at packing, route selection or settlement. Save the parcel reference so the figures can be matched later.

sections.heading: Diagnose an unexpectedly expensive result
paragraphs: Start with the biggest physical change. A seller’s 30-centimetre shoebox placed across the width of a larger carton may force a new outer dimension even when it adds very little scale weight. Look next at the route. A parcel that exceeds a size threshold may have fewer eligible options than a smaller one. Finally compare currency, destination and whether the amount covers only international delivery. These checks often resolve a disagreement between two screenshots without requiring any assumptions about rate changes.

If you still cannot explain the difference, give support one compact comparison. Include your parcel reference, destination, selected route, measurements and dated quote. Say which amount appeared at submission and which amount you expected from the calculator. Ask which input or rule accounts for the difference. A precise question about one parcel gives the reader something they can check, and gives you a better basis for estimating your next shipment.

title: CSSBuy parcel consolidation: what to pack together and what to keep separate
summary: Work through a mixed parcel of shoes, clothing and a fragile accessory, with practical instructions for the warehouse.

sections.heading: Begin with what must arrive intact
paragraphs: Set the cardboard boxes aside for a moment and list the things you expect to receive. A gift may consist of the shoes, their branded box and the printed insert. A pair of trainers for everyday wear may require only the shoes and their spare laces. The physical purchase looks identical in the warehouse, yet one buyer can discard significant packaging while the other would lose part of the gift. Make those decisions item by item before requesting a combined parcel.

CSSBuy describes consolidation on its forwarding pages, together with options for compression and protection. Read the choices actually available for your parcel when you submit it. Decide where you would accept a lower volume and where you would accept a larger carton to reduce damage. If you have a strict spending ceiling, write that down separately. An instruction like “protect everything and make it cheap” gives the packer no basis for choosing between competing priorities.

sections.heading: Sort goods by their packing needs
paragraphs: Imagine a warehouse holding two cotton shirts, a structured cap and a ceramic mug. The shirts can bend around another object. The cap needs space above its crown. The mug brings hard edges, a handle and breakage risk. Placing the three types in the same parcel might be reasonable if the mug has an adequate inner box and the cap can sit away from it. Listing all four objects by their weight alone hides the reason this packing decision needs attention.

For each item, note its rigid dimensions, whether pressure could deform it, and what protection it already has. A boxed accessory may have been held in place by a fitted insert that was easy to miss in the listing photo. Ask for clarification before requesting removal. Keep small loose pieces with the correct product. A detachable cable, mounting screw or spare buckle may weigh almost nothing but its absence can make the received item unusable.

sections.heading: Decide whether to wait for another order
paragraphs: Consolidation can reduce repeated packaging and can change how a route prices a group of items. Waiting introduces a different cost, often measured in time. Write down which orders have actually arrived, which are still with a seller, and the latest day you can start international shipment. Check the account for any relevant storage deadline or paid extension before deciding to wait. A projected domestic delivery date and a confirmed warehouse receipt describe different points in the journey.

Suppose a jacket is already in the warehouse and a second seller has yet to send a small belt. You could wait and fit the belt beside the jacket, or release the jacket now because you need it for a trip. Estimate the combined parcel and the two separate parcels using the same destination and realistic packaging. Then ask how much the lower quoted option saves in exchange for an unknown wait. If that saving is small relative to your deadline, the decision can be straightforward.

sections.heading: Test the space occupied by the most awkward item
paragraphs: Take the longest, widest or least flexible item as your starting point for a rough layout. A poster tube may force a long carton regardless of how little it weighs. A second small item might fit alongside the tube without changing the outside dimensions. Conversely, two shallow retail boxes that stack neatly on paper may exceed a route limit when the protective outer carton is added. Give yourself room for padding wherever surfaces or corners need it.

Use actual measurements wherever possible. Consider a rigid gift box with an exterior footprint of 32 by 22 centimetres and a cap whose crown must stand upright. If the cap sits above the gift box, their heights may effectively add. If they must sit side by side, one of the horizontal dimensions grows. Sketch both arrangements and compare their approximate outer dimensions. No sketch guarantees a warehouse packing result, but it will help you ask a specific question about the dimension most likely to change the quote.

sections.heading: Choose where compression helps
paragraphs: Soft garments can sometimes occupy less space when packed more tightly. CSSBuy lists vacuum packaging among its forwarding services. Think about the material, trim and intended use before selecting it. A plain cotton sweatshirt and a structured jacket with decorative hardware may respond quite differently to pressure. If the item is delicate, ask what protection the warehouse can offer and whether the garment can be kept separate from hard objects. A small decrease in volume may be a poor trade for permanent creasing.

Consider what happens when the parcel is opened at home. A shirt you will wash and iron is easy to restore. A rigid hat intended as a gift or a collector box expected in pristine condition can be difficult to repair. Include an instruction about only the item that matters, such as keeping the cap upright and avoiding compression on its crown. The packer can act on that detail more reliably than on a general request to make the package look nice.

sections.heading: Write packing instructions someone else can execute
paragraphs: Use the warehouse order reference or a distinct item description at the beginning of each request. A useful note for the example parcel might read, “Keep the mug in its protective inner box. Keep the cap upright. The two shirts can be folded. Please tell me if protecting the cap requires a larger carton.” The instruction identifies each object, states what the buyer permits and gives the packer a reason to ask before making a change.

Distinguish between the outer delivery carton and a retail box you want to retain. Mention any fitted inserts, accessories or paperwork you expect to keep. If you are considering a split shipment, say which objects should stay together and why. A matching pair of accessories that must reach the same recipient is a poor candidate for a split unless the recipient understands the plan. Save a copy of the instruction and update it if an item is removed after inspection.

sections.heading: Compare complete packing proposals
paragraphs: Once you have enough measurement information, compare the cost and feasibility of two specific plans. Plan A might keep all items together with the mug protected in its own inner box. Plan B might send clothing and cap in one parcel and the mug separately. Obtain route estimates for both parcels in Plan B and add them. Looking at the cheaper of the two separate quotes leaves out the parcel that still has to travel. Record any selected packing charges alongside the respective plan.

If two proposals have nearly the same cost, consider the consequences of delay or damage. A separate parcel can arrive on a different day and needs its own tracking record. A combined parcel makes the recipient check one delivery but ties all items to that shipment. Also confirm that each proposed combination is actually eligible for the route you intend to use. Packaging cannot turn an ineligible item into an eligible one.

sections.heading: Inspect the final inventory before release
paragraphs: Before paying for the international shipment, read the selected order references aloud against your list. Check quantities and the warehouse status for each item. Resolve a disputed colour, missing accessory or other open issue before treating that purchase as ready to ship. Keep the domestic references somewhere you can recover them even after the order has been assigned to a parcel. A photo of the item may help you recognise it, but the reference makes it easier to trace a specific purchase.

After delivery, open the parcel carefully enough to preserve evidence of how it was packed if anything has shifted or broken. Account for small accessories before recycling the filler. Keep a short note about which packaging choices worked and which changed the dimensions more than expected. That record is especially valuable when buying the same kind of object again. You are building a personal reference for your own boxes, destinations and priorities, grounded in things you have actually received.

title: What does a CSSBuy order really cost? Build a budget for both shipping legs
summary: Follow a worked two-seller example from checkout to delivery, separating actual payments, estimates and parcel-level costs.

sections.heading: Give the budget one clear purpose
paragraphs: A product discovery page can tell you whether a sweater is worth a closer look. A purchase budget answers a different question. How much money is likely to leave your pocket before that particular sweater reaches you, alongside anything else you plan to order? Start by naming the items and destination. State whether you are trying to assess the price of a single item shipped alone, the marginal cost of adding it to an existing parcel, or its share of a combined purchase. Those are three legitimate calculations with different answers.

Use one working currency for the arithmetic. You can display a second currency for convenience, but keep the original amounts as recorded by the seller, agent or carrier. When you compare yesterday’s screenshot with today’s checkout, an exchange-rate movement can otherwise look like a price increase. Write the date beside the conversion and leave enough room to record what your payment provider actually charged. A catalogue currency selector is helpful for browsing and does not settle the exchange rate on a separate payment.

sections.heading: Follow the first shipping leg to the warehouse
paragraphs: CSSBuy’s Buy For Me guide describes paying for an item and its delivery within China before the warehouse stage. Record merchandise price, quantity and domestic delivery separately for each seller order. This makes a difference when one seller charges a single local delivery amount for several units and another charges separately. If the seller changes the quote because you selected a larger variant or a different quantity, replace the earlier amount rather than retaining both in your total.

Here is a fictional purchase written in yuan solely to illustrate the arithmetic. Seller A offers two shirts at 80 each with 10 for delivery to the warehouse. Seller B offers a bag at 120 with 8 for its own domestic delivery. Merchandise comes to 280. The first freight leg totals 18, so the running purchase cost is 298. A buyer who describes the bag as costing 120 is reporting its merchandise price accurately. A buyer who budgets 120 as the entire amount to receive the bag is missing several stages.

sections.heading: Give every extra charge a home
paragraphs: Create one row per confirmed service or transaction charge, using its actual label and currency. Possible places to look are the order confirmation, the account payment record and the parcel submission screen. Some charges relate to a specific item and some to the parcel as a whole. Include only services you actually selected or amounts the provider actually displays. An optional service shown in a menu contributes zero to your chosen plan until you select it.

Continue the fictional example with 12 for a set of selected services on the combined order. The working subtotal becomes 310 before international shipping. Suppose the account statement records a payment covering both the 298 purchase and those 12 of services. The statement is evidence that 310 was paid. It does not create another 310 of costs. Keep a column for the source of each figure so you can reconcile the itemised budget with a combined payment record.

sections.heading: Treat the international parcel as its own purchase
paragraphs: The second freight leg begins with the package that will leave the warehouse. Get the amount from a calculation or submission for the final destination and the packing arrangement you want. Keep the quote date, route and assumptions beside it. A parcel that includes the two shirts and the bag may have a different size and chargeable weight from a parcel of shirts alone. An earlier shipping quote for a similarly priced product gives you little information about this package.

Suppose the buyer enters a provisional international shipping figure of 90 for the combined shipment. The budget now stands at 400. Later the final amount for that leg is 84. Replace 90 with 84 to obtain 394, or show a 90 deposit followed by a six-unit credit if that is what the account actually records. Both methods yield the same result when used consistently. Adding the deposit and the final amount as independent costs would incorrectly tell the buyer that this order cost 484.

sections.heading: Decide how to handle destination-side amounts
paragraphs: There may be costs that the seller and warehouse do not quote on the product page. Inspect what the selected service explicitly includes and what remains payable separately. For country-specific duties or taxes, consult your destination’s official guidance using the relevant goods and purchase value. Leave a clearly labelled unknown where the facts do not support a number. Zero should mean that you have a reason for entering zero, rather than that a web form left a box empty.

If a delivery provider later collects a documented amount, put it in a separate row and retain the receipt. In the worked example, an additional actual payment of 20 would bring 394 to 414 in the same working currency. That is an arithmetic illustration and assigns no tax rule to any country or product. If settlement occurs in a different currency, show the original payment and the conversion method. Someone reviewing the record can then distinguish a new fee from a difference caused by conversion.

sections.heading: Compare the incremental cost of one more item
paragraphs: There are two useful quotes if you are deciding whether to add the bag. Obtain one estimate for the parcel containing only the shirts and another for the same parcel plan with the bag added. Hold destination and route assumptions constant whenever both combinations remain eligible. The difference in estimated international shipping is the marginal freight relevant to this choice. Add the bag’s own merchandise price, its domestic freight and any item-specific service charges to that difference.

For instance, if the shirts-only parcel would cost 70 internationally and the combined parcel is estimated at 90, the extra international freight for adding the bag is 20. With the fictional 120 price and eight local delivery amount, the marginal outlay is 148 before other changes. If the bag forces a different route or a destination-side charge, recalculate using the feasible option and include the difference. A simple “international shipping divided by three items” calculation answers how to share the cost after purchase, a separate question.

sections.heading: Split a real parcel bill fairly
paragraphs: Decide how to allocate a shared charge before asking anyone else to pay. A flat split per unit is easy to explain when the items are similar. A share based on packed weight may suit several dense items of comparable shape. If a large, light item is responsible for most of the box volume, a weight-only split may assign its freight to someone else. In that case compare alternative quotes with and without that item or agree another allocation everyone understands.

Apply the same rule to credits and refunds as to the original charge. If three people contributed equally to a deposit, record how a later credit is divided. Be explicit about an account credit that remains in one person’s balance rather than arriving in a bank account. The parcel’s cost has changed, but the group may still need a separate settlement. Keep personal addresses, payment information and account records outside any product spreadsheet intended for sharing.

sections.heading: Close the record when the order is complete
paragraphs: Line up the marketplace or CSSBuy order references, the domestic delivery records and the international parcel number. Check that each amount counted once, that cancelled items were removed or credited, and that the quantities received match what the budget describes. If a replacement item travelled separately, give it its own freight line. Folding a replacement into the old parcel without mentioning the second shipment makes the next estimate look inexplicably high.

Keep a short explanation of the largest difference between your first budget and the settled total. Perhaps you retained a retail box, added another item, chose a faster route or discovered that two domestic shipments were billed separately. One sentence about that cause is more useful for future buying than a single average shipping percentage. It tells you which input you need to establish earlier next time, while leaving genuine changes in rates and circumstances open.

title: CSSBuy Buy For Me vs Ship For Me: which order should you create?
summary: Choose the correct workflow by identifying who paid the seller, where the domestic tracking number comes from and what the warehouse still needs.

sections.heading: Start with the seller transaction
paragraphs: The fastest way to choose between CSSBuy Buy For Me and Ship For Me is to answer one practical question. Who is placing the order with the original seller? In Buy For Me, you give CSSBuy the item and option instructions so the agent can purchase for you. In Ship For Me, you have made or will make the purchase yourself and want CSSBuy to receive and forward it. Both can lead to goods waiting at a warehouse. The records required to get them there differ from the first step.

Look at what you already possess. A saved Weidian product link and a screenshot of a size choice mean you have identified an item. A marketplace order confirmation and a successful payment mean a purchase has already taken place. A tracking number is evidence about a shipment, which may be issued later. Mixing up those three stages can lead to asking an agent to buy something you already own, or entering a product ID where the forwarding form asks for tracking.

sections.heading: When you want CSSBuy to purchase the item
paragraphs: Open the original listing and identify the intended variant before visiting the ordering screen. Give the agent enough information to distinguish your choice from adjacent options. For clothing, that could be the seller’s exact colour name, labelled size and quantity. If two options show the same thumbnail but have different dimensions or included accessories, record the text that distinguishes them. A screenshot can help explain the instruction, but it is still worth preserving the current seller link and selected option wording.

CSSBuy’s Buy For Me instructions describe entering a product link or searching on the service, selecting options, and paying for the goods and local delivery. Review the order as CSSBuy displays it before confirming. Check the number of units and the option-specific price. A link that opened on the correct product can still default to the first colour or size in the list. If the desired option is missing, ask for clarification while the order is still only a proposal.

sections.heading: When you have already paid the seller
paragraphs: Use the forwarding workflow when you take responsibility for the marketplace checkout and need the parcel associated with your CSSBuy warehouse record. Open your own account and copy the current personalised warehouse address and recipient details as shown there. Use those details when arranging domestic delivery with the seller. Keep the marketplace confirmation in your own records. Public instructions can describe the process, but another customer’s address screenshot cannot supply your account-specific information.

The CSSBuy forwarding form asks for product information and the domestic shipping company, tracking number and quantity. Have the seller’s dispatch record available as you enter these details. Copy the number issued for the actual delivery to the warehouse. The number embedded in the storefront URL identifies a product and may be the same for hundreds of buyers. It cannot tell a warehouse which of many packages from that seller belongs to you. Update the record or contact support if the seller changes carrier after creating a label.

sections.heading: Walk through the same purchase both ways
paragraphs: Consider a shopper who wants one navy canvas bag with a long strap. In the first version, the shopper has found the bag but has not paid. They open the CSSBuy ordering flow, verify that the pictured option actually includes the long strap, specify navy and one unit, and review the price for delivery to the warehouse. Their CSSBuy purchase record is now the natural place to check what instruction the agent received. If the seller asks whether a shorter strap is acceptable, the buyer can decide before accepting the change.

In the second version, the shopper has already bought the navy bag on the marketplace and given the seller the personalised warehouse address. This time they open the forwarding form, enter the product details and record the seller’s domestic carrier and tracking when available. There is no need to request another purchase. If the wrong strap turns up, the marketplace confirmation is the evidence of what the buyer ordered from the seller. The forwarding record helps establish what the warehouse received and which parcel it belongs to.

sections.heading: Prepare for split or combined domestic dispatch
paragraphs: One marketplace order can produce more than one physical shipment. A seller might send the in-stock item today and an accessory later. Keep both tracking numbers with the order record, together with an item-by-item description of what each parcel should contain. Check how the forwarding form or support team wants those deliveries registered. Seeing one tracking number marked delivered should prompt you to check which part arrived before concluding that the whole order is available to ship onward.

The reverse also occurs when a seller places several purchases into one domestic package. Record the tracking number once in your own inventory and list the expected contents underneath it. Follow the current account instructions for associating those contents with the warehouse receipt. Creating several contradictory declarations about the same tracked carton can complicate reconciliation. If the warehouse record shows one item where you expected two, provide the references and contents list so the discrepancy can be checked.

sections.heading: Handle a missing, unclear or changed listing
paragraphs: A product that cannot be imported into the standard purchase page may still have a usable original seller link. CSSBuy’s Buy For Me guide points readers to an assisted option for items that ordinary search does not find. Preserve the supplier page and give an exact description of the variant you want. Ask about availability and the current price rather than copying an old figure from a spreadsheet. Wait for the agent’s response before assuming that a similar-looking listing is interchangeable.

A forwarding order has a different failure point. If the seller has removed the listing after you paid, your purchase confirmation and dispatch receipt remain important. Keep a copy of the original option text, quantity and seller’s order reference. Ask CSSBuy what information it needs to identify the incoming delivery. If there is a seller dispute, use the actual marketplace purchase record as your starting point. Opening a fresh agent purchase for the replacement changes the transaction and should be a deliberate choice.

sections.heading: Bring the two workflows together at inspection
paragraphs: Once the goods have been received and associated with your account, inspect the visible information for the actual item. Confirm quantity, option and any accessories that affect your acceptance decision. Compare the received colour name or label with the order record, and use photos when they help resolve an uncertainty. If part of the order is missing, ask about that specific part before instructing the warehouse to prepare the parcel. An international shipment makes a simple domestic clarification more difficult.

Keep domestic and international tracking clearly labelled from this point onward. Your seller’s domestic shipment ends at the warehouse. The international parcel you later create can contain goods from multiple sellers or from different purchase dates. Record which warehouse order references were selected and which international parcel they joined. Someone checking delivery progress later should be able to tell immediately whether a tracking update describes the seller-to-warehouse leg or the parcel on its way to the recipient.

sections.heading: Use the record to choose your next action
paragraphs: If your only evidence is an interesting listing, the next task is to confirm the desired product and decide who will place the order. If you have paid but the seller has not dispatched, check the marketplace order and wait for the appropriate dispatch details. If the seller has dispatched to your personalised warehouse address, focus on matching the incoming tracking to your forwarding record. When the item is visible in your warehouse account, turn your attention to inspection and onward packing.

This sequence also makes support messages shorter. Include the relevant marketplace or CSSBuy order reference, the stage that has been reached and the single discrepancy you want checked. For example, explain that the marketplace shows two parcels, one warehouse item has appeared, and the second tracking number still lacks a matching receipt. The recipient can investigate a specific handoff. You can then choose your next step without placing a duplicate order or paying for an onward parcel that is still incomplete.
